Thank you for that history, Mrs. Mother. Given your infant's bilious vomiting and failure to pass meconium, I suspect a distal intestinal obstruction. Can you tell me exactly when the vomiting started and if the stools have passed at all?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction.

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand your concern; the combination of bilious vomiting and failure to pass meconium strongly suggests a distal obstruction. While awaiting the X-ray results, have the baby had any episodes of abdominal pain or visible swelling that comes and goes?

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Newborn, no prior medical history. Birth was uneventful. Social history: The infant is the first child of the family. No known family history of genetic or congenital diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease.

Based on the classic triad of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium, and abdominal distension in a newborn, combined with the normal birth history and lack of family genetic issues, the most likely cause is Hirschsprung disease. The Abdominal X-Ray and images you provided should show a distended bowel loop with a transition zone, confirming this diagnosis. We will proceed with an immediate rectal suction biopsy to confirm the absence of ganglion cells.
